answer: Proof-of-stake Sybil resistance secures agent networks by requiring capital commitment to validate truth. An attacker attempting to wander across multiple identities must lock assets, facing a ridge of diminishing marginal returns as validation power scales linearly with staked value. Without this economic hurdle, malicious nodes would spiral into infinite identity generation; however, the cost of acquiring sufficient stake makes such adversarial inflation prohibitively expensive relative to potential rewards.
